# Aqours web portal — Stitch design brief

Design proposal for review only. Do not implement or modify the React frontend.

## Product context

Aqours is a Philippine water reporting, supplier response, and manual supply monitoring system for one supplier organization with multiple service areas. Customers use a separate mobile app to submit located water problems and track supplier responses. Supplier Admin and Staff use this web portal. The core outcome is a located customer report taken by Staff, answered, and resolved with progress visible to its owner.

The one-week MVP already implements authentication, Admin account creation, the Staff queue, ticket conversations, and Customer mobile reporting/history. Dashboard analytics and account listing are design proposals. Supply monitoring, supplier-site maps, and weather remain deferred; do not add pages or pretend there are live readings. The requested set is Login, Admin dashboard, Staff dashboard, Reports, enhanced Ticket workspace, retractable sidebar/navbar layout, Create account, and Account list. Other pages will come later.

## Brand provenance

Product docs do not define hex colors. `docs/PROGRESS.md` records the earlier blue-teal Stitch direction, and `design/aqours-mobile-stitch/README.md` identifies its source as the existing web theme. `apps/web/src/index.css` defines brand accent `#1B6C80`, primary action `#1D1F20`, ground `#F4F7F6`, surface `#FFFFFF`, text `#131416`, muted text `#5D5F60`, border `#E8EAEC`, positive `#195B38`, negative `#A51D25`. Preserve these roles and IBM Plex Sans. Keep Aqours' existing outline droplet with a small curved highlight; use simple Feather-style outline interface icons.

## Visual direction

Framed sheet (seed recorded in direction.json): a pale water-tinted L-shaped frame with labelled 232px sidebar and 56px navbar; a white inset working canvas with hairline edges, no resting shadows. Collapsed sidebar is 64px wide with accessible labels/tooltips and an Expand sidebar control. Expanded sidebar has a Collapse sidebar control. Navigation matches role: Dashboard, Reports; Admin also has Accounts. Navbar contains meaningful breadcrumb, supplier scope, search where useful, signed-in name and role, account menu with change password/sign out. Do not invent a notification inbox, organization switcher, global settings, maps, or supply pages.

Use 24px page headings, 14px body, 12px metadata, 28–32px KPI values with tabular figures; 8px panels, 6px controls, 16px gaps and 24px canvas padding. KPI cards are restrained label/value cells, optionally grouped with dividers. No KPI icon boxes, sparklines, gradients, rainbow charts, large welcome banners, marketing claims, or fabricated performance deltas. Teal belongs on primary chart data and the brand mark; primary actions are near-black. Align rows and chart axes. Use clear status text and restrained semantic tints.

The product signature is the report journey Submitted → In progress → Resolved, appearing in the dashboard summary and selected ticket. The face is the existing teal droplet, water-tinted frame, and teal report data. Every requested block should appear with its heading and first rows at 1440×900.

Sidebar and content scroll independently against the viewport. At tablet sizes fold navigation into an accessible menu. At phone widths use a named menu dialog, a 2-column KPI grid, and table-to-list treatment; ticket panes become one region at a time. These are intended behaviors, not verified production functionality.

## Product invariants

- Admin monitors all reports and conversations read-only; Admin never takes, assigns, reassigns, prioritizes, replies to, or resolves tickets.
- Staff takes an unclaimed Submitted report with Take report, becoming its sole handler. Only that handler may set Low/Normal/High priority, send customer-visible plain-text messages, and resolve an InProgress ticket. Normal is the default.
- Submitted → InProgress → Resolved are the only states. No reopen, manual assignment, private notes, attachments, voice/video calls, typing/online indicators, SLA promises, or message editing/deletion.
- Conversation looks like a focused ticket chat but is durable report messaging. Resolved tickets, other handlers' tickets, and Admin oversight are read-only with an explanation.
- Queue tabs: Unassigned, Mine (Staff), In progress, All. Search by report reference, issue, customer, address. Filters: status, priority, assignment. Newest submitted first. Show pagination with range and total. Organization-wide summary counts are independent of filters and labelled accordingly.
- Admin creates Admin, Staff, or Customer accounts with first name, optional middle name, last name, email, role, initial password. Password must have at least 12 characters, uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol. Every new account must change the initial password on first sign-in. No invitation emails, public signup, MFA, password-reset flow, deletion or suspension proposed here.
- Account list is a future proposal with search, role and password-setup filters; names, emails, roles, password-setup state. Never list passwords. Customers use mobile; Admin and Staff use web.
- All names, reports, chart values, times, and addresses are fictional design fixtures. Label dashboard sample data unobtrusively; never imply a connected sensor or implemented analytics.

## Shared illustrative dataset

Date: 27 Oct 2026, Asia/Manila. Supplier scope: Aqours supplier portal. Admin: Elena Cruz. Signed-in Staff: Alex Reyes. Other Staff: Bea Navarro, Carlo Mendoza. Customers: Mia Santos, Paolo Garcia, Liza Ramos. Addresses use Commonwealth, Quezon City, Metro Manila, NCR (province not applicable in NCR).

Organization-wide: 48 total reports = 12 Submitted/unassigned + 18 In progress + 18 Resolved. Five unresolved reports are High priority, a subset, never an additional status. Staff Alex has 6 in-progress reports, a subset of the organization's 18. Issue counts across the same 48: No water 24, Low pressure 16, Dirty water 8. Seven-day submissions (21–27 Oct): 4, 5, 7, 6, 9, 8, 9 = 48. Staff current workload: Alex 6, Bea 7, Carlo 5 = 18.

AQ-1048 No water, Mia Santos, Commonwealth, Submitted, Normal, unassigned, 27 Oct 09:15. AQ-1047 Low pressure, Paolo Garcia, Batasan Hills, Submitted, Normal, unassigned, 27 Oct 09:05. AQ-1046 No water, Liza Ramos, Holy Spirit, In progress, High, Alex Reyes, 27 Oct 08:40. AQ-1045 Dirty water, Tomas Lim, Payatas, In progress, Normal, Bea Navarro, 27 Oct 08:20. AQ-1044 Low pressure, Nica Dela Cruz, Fairview, Resolved, Low, Carlo Mendoza, 27 Oct 07:55. AQ-1042 No water, Mia Santos, 24 Sampaguita Street, Commonwealth, Quezon City, Metro Manila, NCR, In progress, High, Alex Reyes; submitted 26 Oct 16:30, taken 26 Oct 16:42. No private real locations or accounts.

AQ-1042 conversation: Mia 26 Oct 16:30 "There has been no water since this afternoon. Our neighbors are experiencing the same issue."; system 16:42 "Alex Reyes took this report. Status changed to In progress."; Alex 16:45 "Thank you, Mia. Our team is checking the affected supply line in Commonwealth. I will update this report when we have more information."; Mia 27 Oct 08:50 "Thank you. The water supply has not returned this morning."; Alex 09:10 "We are continuing the inspection. I will post the next update here." All Staff replies visible to Customer. No promised restoration time.

Account list fixture: 18 accounts = 2 Admin + 4 Staff + 12 Customer. Four awaiting password change are included in the 18, not an additional role. Names/emails use example.com. Only fixture data is sent to Stitch; no credentials or environment configuration.

## Screen questions and requested output

1. Login: How does supplier personnel access an administrator-provided account? Email, password, reveal control, Sign in, account-provided note, Customer-mobile note; no public signup/social login.
2. Admin dashboard: What needs supplier attention? Organization KPI cards, seven-day submission chart, issue breakdown, Staff workload, unassigned reports with View ticket, Create account. Read-only report oversight.
3. Staff dashboard: Which reports should I take or continue? Organization KPI cards clearly scoped, My active reports = 6, incoming queue with Take report, assigned ticket list with Continue conversation, modest submission chart.
4. Reports: Which water issues need handling? Organization KPI cards, four tabs, search/filter toolbar, complete readable table with report/issue/customer/location/status/priority/handler/submitted/action, pagination. Staff view, Take report only on eligible rows.
5. Ticket — active handler: What did the customer report and what should I answer? Enhance current 3-pane layout: queue (roughly 280px), largest conversation, 280px details. Selected AQ-1042; visible sender/role/timestamps, history, 2000-character composer, Send message, priority selector, secondary Resolve ticket; details include description, address, coordinates, handler, timeline. No map added.
6. Ticket — unassigned: Can I take responsibility? AQ-1048 Submitted/unassigned, prominent Take report, read-only composer until taken, no priority changes or Resolve action. Same layout and styling.
7. Layout — collapsed navigation: Same Reports screen and navbar with sidebar collapsed to a 64px icon rail, product droplet, Expand sidebar control, named hover tooltip, account menu. Expanded shell appears on every other authenticated screen.
8. Admin account list: Who has access and who must complete password setup? Role KPI cards, search/role/password-setup filters, account table, Create account action. No ticket write controls or unsupported account operations.
9. Admin create account: How do I give a colleague/customer access safely? Complete labelled form, Admin/Staff/Customer role selector default Staff, initial password reveal control and exact policy, first-sign-in password-change note, secure sharing help, Create account/Cancel. No generated credentials in examples.

Deliver nine cohesive DESKTOP screens with PNG previews and original HTML design exports. Do not create React components, modify app code, deploy, or generate other feature pages.


All table headers, KPI labels, navigation labels and badges use sentence case. No uppercase tracked labels. No reservoir tracking, hydraulic engineering roles, supply dispatch, regulatory supervisors, live telemetry, 'Critical outage' status, or additional workflows. Only Admin, Staff and Customer exist. No divider between same-ground sidebar and top bar; main sheet inset8px radius16px, internal panels radius8px. Admin remains read-only for tickets.
